heroSummary: The Bambu Lab P1P achieves a reliable maximum speed of 214 mm/s at an 18 mm³/s volumetric limit with eSUN ABS+, but its open-frame design makes an aftermarket enclosure or draft shield essential to prevent severe warping. While the stock stainless steel nozzle handles this non-abrasive blend easily, thermal management around the print bed is the primary engineering bottleneck.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate + PVP Glue Stick or Liquid Bed Adhesive (98°C)
slicerTweaks: Cap Max Volumetric Speed at 18 mm³/s in the filament profile and lower outer wall speed to 120 mm/s to preserve layer adhesion and surface finish.
Set Bed Temperature to 98°C (near the 100°C hardware ceiling) and disable the auxiliary cooling fan entirely to prevent localized thermal shock.
Enable a 5mm outer brim with 0.0mm brim-object gap to mechanically resist corner lifting on larger functional parts.
Adjust Part Cooling Fan settings to min 10% and max 25%, with fan disabled for the first 4 layers and activated only on overhangs exceeding 50%.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Corner lifting and bed detachment (thermal warping)
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: The open-frame P1P allows cool room drafts to induce rapid thermal contraction across the ABS part geometry.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Install an enclosure or temporary draft shield, heat the bed to 98°C, apply liquid glue, and enable an 8mm outer brim.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Interlayer splitting / delamination under mechanical stress
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive part cooling or excessive print speed causing the extruded bead to chill before cross-linking polymer chains.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Increase nozzle temperature to 255°C, turn off the auxiliary fan completely, and limit part cooling fan to a 15% ceiling.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Rough extrusion surface and micro-popping (moisture contamination)
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: eSUN ABS+ is hygroscopic and absorbed ambient moisture, flashing into micro-steam bubbles inside the 250°C hotend melt zone.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the spool in a dedicated filament dryer at 65°C to 70°C for 6 to 8 hours before printing, then feed from a sealed dry box.

faq.question: Can I print eSUN ABS+ on a stock Bambu Lab P1P without an enclosure?
faq.answer: Small parts under 40mm can print successfully using a draft shield and brim, but larger parts will warp or delaminate without a full enclosure.

faq.question: Do I need to upgrade to a hardened steel nozzle for eSUN ABS+?
faq.answer: No, eSUN ABS+ contains no abrasive fibers or particles, so the P1P's stock stainless steel nozzle is completely safe to use.

faq.question: Why is the print speed limited to 214 mm/s when the P1P can hit 500 mm/s?
faq.answer: At standard 0.2mm layer height and 0.42mm line width, 214 mm/s reaches the maximum safe 18 mm³/s flow threshold of the hotend to prevent underextrusion.

faq.question: What is the optimal bed temperature considering the P1P's 100°C hardware limit?
faq.answer: Set the bed temperature to 98°C, which delivers sufficient thermal energy to stay near the glass transition point of ABS+ without triggering thermal runaway protection.
